lineas.texto: Part two. Today is market day, and the whole village walks to town.
By law, a new market could not open within about seven miles of another one.
At the town gate, you pay a small toll just to come in.
The streets are loud and muddy. Pigs wander between the stalls.
Above each shop hangs a picture: a boot, a loaf, a key. Most people cannot read.
You sell your eggs and cheese, and buy the one thing you cannot make at home: salt.
Be careful who you trust. A baker caught cheating could be locked in the pillory.
Before dark, a bell rings the curfew. Cover your fire. The gates are closing.
